blocks.text: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI, 1935)** is the **central bank** — banker to the government, issuer of currency, and manager of **monetary policy** to control inflation and support growth, now under a **flexible inflation-targeting** framework.

rows: Central bank; nationalised **1949**; functions — currency issue, banker's bank, monetary policy, forex, regulator.
**MPC (6 members)** sets the **repo rate**; targets **CPI inflation 4% ±2%**.
**Repo & reverse repo, CRR, SLR, MSF, OMO, Bank Rate**.
**Dear money (contractionary)** to curb inflation; **cheap money (expansionary)** to boost growth.
Flexible IT framework since **2016** (RBI Act amended).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: RBI & monetary policy

items: **RBI (est. 1935, nationalised 1949)**: functions — note issue (except ₹1 & coins by Govt), banker to govt & banks, monetary authority, forex manager, regulator/supervisor of banks & NBFCs, lender of last resort.
**Monetary policy**: since 2016 set by the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC, 6 members)** targeting **CPI inflation of 4% (±2%)** — flexible inflation targeting.
**Quantitative tools**: **Repo & Reverse Repo (LAF), CRR, SLR, MSF, Bank Rate, OMO**; **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)**.
**Qualitative tools**: margin requirements, moral suasion, priority-sector lending, credit rationing.
**Stance**: accommodative/neutral/tightening to control **inflation vs growth**; transmission via banks.
RBI (1935, nationalised 1949); MPC sets repo rate; CPI target 4% ±2%.
Tools: repo, CRR, SLR, MSF, OMO; raising repo/CRR = contractionary.

sections.heading: Banking & financial-sector reforms; commercial banks & NPAs

blocks.text: India's **banking system** — led by public-sector banks after **nationalisation (1969)** — has undergone major **reforms (Narasimham Committees)**, and today grapples with **Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)** while expanding **financial inclusion**.

rows: **14 banks in 1969, 6 in 1980**; expanded rural banking.
**(1991 & 1998)** — banking-sector reforms (prudential norms, capital adequacy, autonomy).
Loans not repaid (>90 days); addressed via **SARFAESI Act, IBC (2016), asset reconstruction, recapitalisation**.
**Scheduled commercial banks (public, private, foreign, RRBs), cooperative banks, SFBs, payment banks**.
**Jan Dhan, business correspondents, differentiated banks, UPI/digital**.

items: **Structure**: **Scheduled** (in 2nd Schedule of RBI Act) — commercial (PSBs, private, foreign, RRBs) & cooperative; **NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM, NHB** (development finance); Payment & Small Finance Banks.
**Bank nationalisation**: 1969 (14 banks) & 1980 (6) — priority-sector lending, financial inclusion; recent **PSB mergers** (12 PSBs now).

**NPAs (Non-Performing Assets)**: loans overdue >90 days; twin-balance-sheet problem; resolution via **IBC (2016) & NCLT**, SARFAESI Act, Asset Reconstruction Companies, the **'Bad Bank' (NARCL)**, PCA framework, recapitalisation.
**Financial inclusion**: **PM Jan Dhan Yojana (2014)**, BSBDA, BC model, JAM; India Stack/UPI (world-leading digital payments), Basel III capital norms.
Nationalisation 1969 (14) & 1980 (6); Narasimham Committees (1991, 1998).
NPA resolution: SARFAESI, IBC 2016, recapitalisation; NPA = overdue >90 days.

sections.heading: Financial markets, instabilities, stock exchanges & SEBI

blocks.text: **Financial markets** channel savings to investment through the **money market (short-term)** and **capital market (long-term)**. India's **stock exchanges (BSE, NSE)** are regulated by **SEBI**, guarding against instability and protecting investors.

rows: Short-term (<1 yr) — **T-bills, call money, commercial paper, certificates of deposit**; RBI-regulated.
Long-term — **equity & debt (shares, bonds, debentures)**; primary (IPO) & secondary markets.
**Securities & Exchange Board of India** — regulator of the securities market; statutory 1992.
**Bubbles, crashes, scams (Harshad Mehta 1992)**; SEBI ensures transparency.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: financial markets & SEBI

items: **Money market** (short-term, <1 yr — T-bills, call money, CPs, CDs; RBI-regulated) vs **Capital market** (long-term — equity & debt).
**Capital market**: **primary** (IPO/FPO) & **secondary** (stock exchanges — **BSE (Asia's oldest, 1875) & NSE**; indices **Sensex (30) & Nifty (50)**).
**SEBI (1988, statutory 1992)**: regulator of the securities market — protects investors, regulates exchanges/intermediaries, curbs insider trading & fraud.
**Instruments**: shares, bonds, debentures, mutual funds, derivatives (futures/options), REITs/InVITs, ETFs; **FPI/FII** flows drive volatility.
**Instabilities**: bubbles/crashes, capital-flow volatility, systemic risk; regulators coordinate via the **FSDC** (chaired by FM).

sections.heading: Tax system, recent changes & GST impact

blocks.text: India's **tax system** comprises **direct taxes (income, corporate)** and **indirect taxes**, the latter now unified under the **Goods and Services Tax (GST, 2017)** — a landmark 'One Nation, One Tax' reform administered by the **GST Council**.

rows: **Income tax, corporate tax**; progressive; burden not shiftable; **CBDT**.
Now mostly **GST**; earlier excise, VAT, service tax; **CBIC**.
**101st Amendment**; subsumed most indirect taxes; **CGST + SGST + IGST**; slabs 0/5/12/18/28%.
**Article 279A**; Union FM + state FMs; recommends rates (cooperative federalism).
**Unified market, reduced cascading, higher compliance; revenue-sharing debates**.

items: **Direct taxes** (on income/wealth — progressive; income tax, corporate tax) vs **Indirect taxes** (on goods/services — regressive; GST, customs).

**GST (1 July 2017, 101st Amendment)**: 'One Nation One Tax'; subsumed excise, service tax, VAT, etc.; **destination-based** consumption tax; **CGST + SGST/UTGST + IGST (interstate)**; slabs **0/5/12/18/28% (+cess)**; governed by the **GST Council (Art 279A)** — cooperative federalism; **GSTN** IT backbone.
**Outside GST**: petroleum, alcohol, electricity, stamp duty (for now).

**Reforms**: **faceless assessment, DTC discussions**, corporate-tax cut (2019, 22%), new personal-tax regime; **tax-GDP ratio** (~11-12% centre) still low; **tax buoyancy**; direct-tax collections rising via digitisation.
Direct (income/corporate, CBDT) vs indirect (GST, CBIC); GST via 101st Amendment (2017).
GST Council (Art 279A); CGST+SGST+IGST; removes tax cascading.

blocks.text: India's **fiscal federalism** divides taxation and spending between the Centre and States (Part XII), with the **Finance Commission** periodically recommending the **sharing of taxes and grants** — the key mechanism of vertical and horizontal fiscal balance.

rows: Constituted every **5 years**; recommends **tax devolution & grants-in-aid**.
**15th FC** — states get **41%** of the divisible pool of central taxes.
**Vertical** (Centre-to-states share); **horizontal** (among states, by formula — population, area, income distance, etc.).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: centre-state finance & Finance Commission

items: **Finance Commission (Art 280)**: constituted every **5 years** by the President; recommends (a) **vertical devolution** — states' share of the **divisible pool** of central taxes (15th FC: **41%**), (b) **horizontal distribution** among states (population, area, income-distance, forest, demography), (c) grants-in-aid, local-body & disaster grants.
**15th FC (N.K. Singh)**: award period 2021-26; used **2011 census**; revenue-deficit & sector-specific grants.
**GST Council (Art 279A)**: shares indirect-tax decisions; GST compensation to states (ended 2022, extended cess).
**Issues**: rising **cesses & surcharges** (not in divisible pool → shrink states' share), borrowing limits (FRBM/Art 293), special-category-status demands (**AP** post-bifurcation).
Finance Commission (Art 280, every 5 yrs); 15th FC gives states 41% of divisible pool.

sections.heading: Public debt, expenditure, fiscal policy & the Budget

blocks.text: **Fiscal policy** — the government's use of **taxation, expenditure and borrowing** — is expressed in the annual **Union Budget**. Key concerns are the **fiscal deficit, public debt sustainability, and FRBM discipline**.

rows: 'Annual Financial Statement'; **Revenue & Capital** accounts; presented on **1 February**.
Internal + external borrowings; sustainability = debt/GDP ratio.
Targets fiscal prudence (fiscal deficit ~3% of GDP goal).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: public finance, deficits & budget

items: **Budget (Art 112 — Annual Financial Statement)**: **Revenue** (recurring) vs **Capital** (asset/liability) accounts; presented **1 February**; **Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account**.

**Deficits**: **Fiscal deficit** (total borrowing = expenditure − non-borrowed receipts), **Revenue deficit** (revenue exp − revenue receipts), **Primary deficit** (fiscal − interest payments); **effective revenue deficit**.
**FRBM Act (2003)**: targets fiscal prudence (fiscal deficit ~3% of GDP goal); escape clauses in crises; N.K. Singh review recommended a debt-anchor.
**Public debt**: internal + external; **fiscal policy** (taxation & spending) manages demand/growth; **counter-cyclical** stance; capex push for multiplier effect.
**Bodies**: **CAG audit, Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee**; medium-term fiscal framework.
Fiscal deficit = total borrowing; primary deficit = fiscal – interest; FRBM Act 2003.
Budget (Art 112) = revenue + capital accounts; presented 1 Feb.
